main_text.head: VIRI STRENUISSIMI, NOBILISSIMI, HUMANISSIMI.
main_text.p: Ritum illud; Ingrato homine terra pejus nîl creat, vix ullas non feriit aures, sed quô minus me feriat totum, monet me Sapiens ille suo ναιρὸν γνῶθι, hanc arripere occasionem, quâ benevolentiam ac beneficentiam vestrā, quam hactenus expertus sum; maxi-me vero dum studiorum nostrorum fundamina jaciendi & sermonis Gallici addiscendi gratia ante aliquot annos extra Patrios ageremus lares, agnoscam; cum eam referre non valeam, imo omnia quae in me collata sunt, enarrare quam Sybillae folia mihi laboriosius foret. Adauget enim illum meritorum vestrorum erga me cumulum, quod beneficia collocaveritis in hominem planè immeritum & nec naturae nec fortunae dono commendabilem, qui, ut hebraeo utar dicendi modo, בן ארם praeter humanam & communem sortem praese ferret nihil, quo benevoli vestri affectus captaret auram. Quid! si memori revolvo pectore curas ac labores vestros, quos mei causa suscipiebatis; ubi diversa valetudine semel atq; iterum premebar sed tandem tamen Castigatoris Divini manum medicam experiebar, qui contra spem & Medici & omnium extremum morbi aculeum pharmacum mihi esse jussit, quo valetudine pristina restituerer: Illud divinae benignitatis, hoc vestrae humanitatis esse agnosco; quod in his valetudina-

page.notes: The opening word is a woodcut initial "T" set into a decorative border; its letter is the likely T. The Greek words "ναιρὸν γνῶθι" are as best read from the scan (probably καιρὸν γνῶθι). The heading is set in capitals with the second line spaced out. The Hebrew phrase "בן ארם" is set in the text as printed; a block of Hebrew type appears after "modo,". Several words are partly cut at the left edge of the scan; no readings were guessed beyond what is visible.
